newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close weaker on battered oils.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close weaker on battered oils.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stock market closed weaker in light trading, reeling from a beating in the oils sector. * Almost all 14 sub-indices fell except for real estate, transports, retail.
Toronto stocks ended weaker in light trading on Thursday, swept lower by a downdraft in the oil and gas sector.
"Toronto committed suicide," said portfolio manager Josef Schachter. "The oils and golds ... got clipped and took the market lower."
Oils took a beating after March Nymex oil lost $0.81 today to close at $23.10 a barrel.
Toronto's heavily weighted golds were also sent lower by softer bullion prices in New York. Comex April gold lost $1.30 an ounce to end at $345.10.
Toronto's key 300 Composite Index fell 40.52 points to 6071.89. Trading was lackluster at 107.3 million shares worth C$1.4 billion.
Almost all of Toronto's 14 sub-indices headed lower except for real estate, transports and retail.
Declines edged out advances 402 to 545 while 276 stocks traded flat.

Schachter forecast the downdraft will continue for the next few sessions, pulling Canada's market lower by another 100 points. However, oils may bounce back as the need for heating continues over the rest of the North American winter season, he said.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---
* Oil firm Canadian Natural Resources Ltd lost 1.95 to reach 34.25 on 2.6 million shares.

* Food services firm Cara Operations Ltd topped Toronto's most active issues, with class A shares gaining 0.35 to close at 4.10 on 6.6 million shares. It had reported positive third quarter earnings and stronger second quarter results from 37-percent owned unit Second Cup Ltd.
* Barrick Gold Corp lost 0.60 to reach 35.25 in active trading.
